title: How We Built an Agent That Improves Itself — Zubin Aysola, Weights & Biases
talk_summary: W&B built an agent (Arya) with a production/offline eval flywheel: every production trace becomes a regression task, run against a bit-identical agent config in a simulated sandbox, scored, and hill-climbed. They YAML-define many parallel agent variants and let the agent itself generate tasks, run evals, and propose prompt/skill fixes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every production miss (and win) is converted into a task in the offline eval framework, so the eval suite grows from real traffic rather than hand-written benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every production miss or every production goodness as well ... becomes a task for our agent framework

takeaways.technique: Bit-identical prod vs offline agent config
takeaways.what_they_do: They run the exact same agent code/config in production and in the simulated eval environment, with a 4-hour sync job to prevent drift between the two.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we benchmark a bite-wise identical version of the agent in our production environment and our simulated environment

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent configurations are declared in YAML so many mutations of the same config can run in parallel and be compared, rather than testing one change at a time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: YAML define different configurations of the agent to sort of get multiple parallel uh variants and then test them all

takeaways.technique: Agent self-improvement loop (trace → task → candidate → score)
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent reviews its own rollout, identifies the root cause (e.g. a missing SDK call), writes a hill-climb target, runs prod vs candidate variants, and reports which scored better.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It identified that the problem was that we weren't calling weave.log ... properly in the sandbox

takeaways.technique: Unconstrained sandbox for emergent parallel execution
takeaways.what_they_do: They give the agent a sandbox where it can do anything, including spawning parallel copies of its own research loop, to enable emergent behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having that unconstrained environment is really useful for getting the agent to do emergent things

takeaways.what_they_do: They score tasks both pass/fail (normative) and comparatively between variants (e.g. asks-questions vs not), a standard RL-style formulation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Arya scores itself in two patterns which is normatively ... and then relativistically
